cleared.check: Task 3. Legacy jump destination analysis (revm-bytecode analyze_legacy) located in each binary by its loop (cmp of the byte with 0x5b, signed compare with 0x60 and an advance of byte minus 0x5e; op-reth amd64 0x4a4a8c0, arm64 0x4229dd8; base amd64 0x831ab10, arm64 0x7447d14) and run in the models with allocation, memset and memcpy modelled, on the PoolManager runtime of this checkout (24,009 bytes), 60 random prefixes of it, 32 programs that end inside PUSH1 to PUSH32, 16 programs that end after STOP, JUMPDEST or the EIP-8024 bytes 0xe6 to 0xe8, the empty program and 400 random programs (seed 3203). The bitmap was compared with the specification and the padded code with analysis.rs of revm-bytecode 42.0.0 and 43.0.0 (the two files are identical).
cleared.result: All 510 programs equal on every binary. For the PoolManager each binary accepts the 610 JUMPDEST bytes outside push data and rejects the 29 inside, and pads the code by one zero byte, as the crate source does. A program that ends inside a PUSH is padded with the missing immediate bytes plus one STOP, so no read runs past the code. The analysed bytecode with its jump table travels inside the Bytecode value; reth's execution cache stores it in code_cache, a fixed_cache::Cache keyed by the full 32-byte code hash, and fixed-cache 0.1.10 returns an entry only when key.equivalent(stored key) holds (lib.rs:322-343), so two codes cannot share an analysis. CachedReads in crates/revm/src/cached.rs:36 and :125-130 is a B256Map keyed by the code hash as well.

cleared.check: Task 4, run live instead of lifted. Nested-frame sequences (seed 3204) over the PoolManager's transient and persistent slot shapes: IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT (Lock.sol:8), NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT (NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10), RESERVES_OF_SLOT and CURRENCY_SLOT (CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13), nine CurrencyDelta keccak slots (CurrencyDelta.sol:10-17), a pool state slot with its next three words and two small constants. Four frames by code override; each frame stores, loads, calls the next by CALL, DELEGATECALL or STATICCALL with fixed gas, and ends by RETURN, REVERT, INVALID or STOP; the outer frame returns every load, call flag and return-data hash and then all slots. Each sequence was run by eth_call and in tools/opdiff/pyevm.py. 15,000 sequences in all.

The two builds with 5,000 sequences, Base and Unichain, each differ on the same sequence (index 2678) and refuse the same one (index 2393, out of gas at 20,000,000). Both come from gas: pyevm has no gas, a callee ending in INVALID consumes all the gas it was given, and the frame that made four such calls ran out. With the innermost call gas lowered from 200,000 to 30,000 the node's answer equals the reference on both (recheck on reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/base/v1.5.6 and op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332/x86_64-linux). A reverted or halted frame restored the previous transient and persistent values, a nested revert was not undone twice, and TSTORE under STATICCALL failed, on every chain and build reached. The binary journal routines themselves were not lifted.

leadResults.answer: The EVM path of the B20 precompile (precompile-storage/src/evm.rs) is byte-identical in base v1.5.6 and v1.6.0-rc.9 and writes every slot through EvmInternals into the revm journal under a checkpoint that is committed or reverted with the call; the token logic is unchanged outside tests. TokenRollbackProbe at the PoolManager address on mainnet.base.org (base v1.5.6) left OUSD balances unchanged in reverted, invalid, call-depth, out-of-gas and static frames and moved exactly the amount in a returning frame.
